passage: At two in the morning in Singapore, Chen typed a long post about how much she hated school, how her parents were being unfair and how she felt like nobody understood her. She added the name of her school and a photo of her uniform. Her thumb hovered over 'Post'. She messaged her friend Oskar: 'Should I put this up?' He replied at once, 'Wait until morning. And take out the school name, strangers can see that.' Chen put the phone face-down. In the morning she deleted the school name and the photo and read the post again. It felt too raw now. She sent it privately to Oskar instead, and they talked at recess about what was actually bothering her.

qa.q: What did Chen add to the post besides her feelings?
qa.a: She added the name of her school and a photo of her uniform.

qa.q: Why was Chen tempted to post at two in the morning?
qa.a: She felt misunderstood and wanted someone to hear how she felt, and the late hour made her feelings seem larger. She may also have wanted attention or support.
He told her to wait until morning, take out identifying details and then talk to him, which let her pause and choose a trusted audience.

qa.q: How might her parents have felt if they had seen the post?
qa.a: They may have felt hurt and worried, and it could have made the conversation harder.

grounding: A teen pauses before posting personal details and feelings, and turns to a trusted friend instead.

passage: Mr Francis wrote on the whiteboard: 'What would you never post?' and gave the class of Year Ten two minutes. Samir, who had posted his home address and a photo of his door key ring the week before to show off a new lock, went quiet. Someone said, 'Your address.' Someone else said, 'When you're really upset.' Francis asked the class, 'If it stays online for years, who might see it?' Samir put his hand up slowly. "Someone could read my old posts when I apply for a course." After class he stayed. "I want to delete the address one. Can you help?" Francis nodded. "Let's do it now. And who would you talk to for the big stuff?" Samir thought. "My cousin."

qa.q: What did Mr Francis write on the whiteboard?
qa.a: He wrote: 'What would you never post?'

qa.q: What was Samir probably feeling when he went quiet?
qa.a: He was probably embarrassed and worried, because he had posted his address and key ring photo, and the discussion made him see the risk. Asking to delete it shows he wanted to fix it.
He asked his teacher to help him delete the post right away and named his cousin as someone to talk to about heavy topics.

qa.q: How might Mr Francis have felt when Samir stayed after class?
qa.a: He may have felt pleased that the lesson reached Samir and that Samir trusted him with the problem.

grounding: A teen learns to consider permanence and audience, and uses trusted people for heavy topics, in a class.
